ingestion.notes: ABSTRACT ONLY. Europe PMC has the author manuscript as free-to-read but doesn't offer its full text for download, so methods, marker genes and subset names beyond the abstract were not read. Re-ingest from the full text (PMC5775029) before using this paper as a marker source.

enhanced_abstract.tldr: Single-cell RNA-seq of ~2,400 enriched human blood cells defines six dendritic cell and four monocyte subtypes, including a new pDC-like DC subset, a split within CD1C+ DCs, and a circulating cDC progenitor.

sections.heading: Goal
sections.body: Resolve the identities of, and relationships between, human blood dendritic cell and monocyte subtypes, whose taxonomy was incomplete.

sections.heading: What they found
sections.body: Six DC and four monocyte subtypes in blood. A new DC subset shares features with plasmacytoid DCs but strongly activates T cells, which redefines what counts as a pDC. The CD1C+ DC subset splits in two. The work also places blastic plasmacytoid DC neoplasia cells relative to healthy DCs and identifies a circulating progenitor of conventional DCs.

key_findings: Four monocyte subtypes and six DC subtypes in human blood
A pDC-like DC subset that potently activates T cells
limitations: Healthy blood only; not tumor tissue
Small number of cells (~2,400) by current standards
This record is based on the abstract alone
enhanced_abstract.why_it_matters: Rule 4 (experimental paper that defines cell types with markers, preferred). A core reference for monocyte and DC subsets, one of the group's focus lineages. The actual marker sets must be extracted from the full text before it can supply annotation rules.

sequencing.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of ~2,400 human blood cells (protocol not read).

clustering.summary: Unbiased clustering is implied by the discovery of subtypes; method not read.

annotation.summary: The paper's contribution is a revised taxonomy of blood DC and monocyte subtypes, which other studies use to label clusters.

trajectory.summary: Identifies a circulating cDC progenitor and relates neoplastic pDC-like cells to healthy DCs; methods not read.
